carousels.hook: Claude trains on every paste by default
carousels.throughline: Free AI tools use your pasted data to train their models—here’s how to stop it and keep customer info private.

reel_beats.hook: Your customer lists train Claude unless you flip this toggle

body.text: Claude’s default setting lets it use pasted data to train its models, so customer lists or private notes can end up in its training set.
Flip the ‘Data Sharing’ toggle in settings to ‘Off’ to stop it, but this may limit some AI features.
Paid plans keep your data private without losing features, so consider upgrading if privacy matters.
Always check settings after updates, because defaults often reset to training mode.

carousels.throughline: Gmail’s Primary tab prioritizes emails with replies—here’s how to trigger that first reply in 24 hours.

reel_beats.hook: One reply moves your email to Gmail’s Primary tab—here’s how

body.text: Gmail’s Primary tab prioritizes emails that get replies, so a single reply boosts your sender score and moves future emails to the top.
Send a short, personal follow-up 24 hours after the first email to trigger that first reply, using a simple question like ‘Did this help?’
Use a clear ‘Reply’ button in your email to guide readers, and test subject lines to find what gets the most replies.
This works because Gmail sees replies as a signal of trust, so one reply can change where your emails land for good.

carousels.hook: Google Ads charges the same for browsers and buyers
carousels.throughline: Google Ads treats browsers and buyers the same—here’s how to fix it and cut wasted spend by 30%.

reel_beats.hook: Google Ads bills you the same for a browser and a buyer—here’s the fix

body.text: Google Ads shows ads to anyone searching, even if they’re just browsing, so use ‘Audience Segments’ to target people ready to buy instead.
Exclude ‘low-intent’ searches like ‘how to’ or ‘best free’ from your campaigns, because these waste budget on people who won’t convert.
Switch to ‘Phrase Match’ to show ads only for searches that mean it, cutting wasted spend by 30% and boosting conversion rates.
Check the ‘Search Terms’ report weekly to cut more waste, because even small changes add up to big savings over time.
